This compound, in turn, is identified as a target of Protein-tyrosine phosphatase LC-PTP. The integration of these relationships implies that thioguanine may exert its effects by modulating the activity of Protein-tyrosine phosphatase LC-PTP, potentially through a direct or indirect interaction. The presence of a clear, well-defined target relationship between thioguanine and the enzyme supports the hypothesis that the drug influences the phosphatase activity, which is a critical step in cellular signaling.
